# Checks

Checks that return a readable failure: equality, nearness, text, optionals and outcomes.

<h2 id="expect"><code>Expect</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Expect(
    condition: bool,
    message: char8[..]
) -> ! TestFailure
```

Fails unless `condition` holds.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Test/Src/Expect.rux#L13)

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type        | Description                    |
| ----------- | ----------- | ------------------------------ |
| `condition` | `bool`      | what must be true              |
| `message`   | `char8[..]` | what it means, for the failure |

**Returns**: nothing, or the failure

<h2 id="expect-equal"><code>ExpectEqual&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func ExpectEqual<T: Display>(
    actual: T,
    expected: T
) -> ! TestFailure
```

Fails unless `actual` equals `expected`, saying both.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Test/Src/Expect.rux#L23)

**Type parameters**

| Name         | Description                            |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------- |
| `T: Display` | a type with `==` that can be displayed |

**Parameters**

| Name       | Type | Description               |
| ---------- | ---- | ------------------------- |
| `actual`   | `T`  | what the code gave        |
| `expected` | `T`  | what it should have given |

**Returns**: nothing, or the failure

<h2 id="expect-not-equal"><code>ExpectNotEqual&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func ExpectNotEqual<T: Display>(
    actual: T,
    unexpected: T
) -> ! TestFailure
```

Fails if `actual` equals `unexpected`.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Test/Src/Expect.rux#L38)

**Type parameters**

| Name         | Description                            |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------- |
| `T: Display` | a type with `==` that can be displayed |

**Parameters**

| Name         | Type | Description                   |
| ------------ | ---- | ----------------------------- |
| `actual`     | `T`  | what the code gave            |
| `unexpected` | `T`  | what it should not have given |

**Returns**: nothing, or the failure

<h2 id="expect-near"><code>ExpectNear</code></h2>

```rux
pub func ExpectNear(
    actual: float64,
    expected: float64,
    tolerance: float64
) -> ! TestFailure
```

Fails unless `actual` is within `tolerance` of `expected`.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Test/Src/Expect.rux#L53)

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type      | Description               |
| ----------- | --------- | ------------------------- |
| `actual`    | `float64` | what the code gave        |
| `expected`  | `float64` | what it should have given |
| `tolerance` | `float64` | how far apart they may be |

**Returns**: nothing, or the failure

<h2 id="expect-text"><code>ExpectText</code></h2>

```rux
pub func ExpectText(
    actual: char8[..],
    expected: char8[..]
) -> ! TestFailure
```

Fails unless `actual` is the same text as `expected`, saying at which byte they part and showing each around it.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Test/Src/Expect.rux#L88)

**Parameters**

| Name       | Type        | Description               |
| ---------- | ----------- | ------------------------- |
| `actual`   | `char8[..]` | what the code gave        |
| `expected` | `char8[..]` | what it should have given |

**Returns**: nothing, or the failure

<h2 id="expect-failure"><code>ExpectFailure&lt;T, E&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func ExpectFailure<T, E>(
    outcome: T ! E,
    message: char8[..]

```

The failure of `outcome`, failing the test when it succeeded.

| Name | Description        |
| ---- | ------------------ |

| Name      | Type        | Description                                    |
| --------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `outcome` | `T ! E`     | what the code gave                             |
